headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while ETFs buy and whales pull BTC off exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it answers the only question that matters before you look at anything else: none of the seven majors here are above their 200-day moving average. BTC at $63,653.85 is 49% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51, ETH is 60.6% off its high, and the small-cap end (ADA at -83.2%, DOGE at -75.7%) shows the damage compounds down the risk curve. No golden crosses anywhere. When one asset is below trend it's a story about that asset; when all seven are below trend, that's the market's own posture, and it's a cautious one regardless of what any single day's candle does.

Momentum tells a quieter story than the trend does. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, almost dead center, neither overbought nor oversold, with MACD below signal. ETH's RSI at 56.3 is the strongest reading on the board even as its price sits 60.6% under its high, and its MACD is also below signal, which is a real divergence worth naming: ETH has managed a 6.36% 30-day gain and a 1.81% weekly gain while every other trend indicator still points down. Compare that to DOGE and BNB, where MACD sits above signal despite prices still 75.7% and 56.4% off their highs, respectively. That's positive short-term momentum inside a longer downtrend, the kind of setup where the tape is resting or turning, not screaming either way.

Positioning is where the crowd's bets show up. Funding across BTC, SOL, XRP, and DOGE all sit at the same flat 11% annualized rate on OKX, cheap enough that longs aren't paying much to stay in the trade. But the long/short account ratios diverge sharply: BTC's 1.15 and ETH's 1.10 are close to balanced, while DOGE's 4.31 and XRP's 2.67 show a crowd heavily tilted long on the smaller names. That imbalance shows up in the liquidation data too. In the last four hours, BTC saw $70.98 million in short liquidations against just $2.74 million in longs, and ETH saw $32.91 million in short liquidations against $5.66 million in longs. Shorts got squeezed hard on the majors while the OI on BTC ($2.12 billion) and ETH ($1.35 billion) shows plenty of money still in the boat.

Flows are the clearest signal on the board today. The BTC spot ETF printed $189.3 million net on 18 Aug 2026, with $238.4 million over the last five sessions, though same_direction_days of 2 means that's not yet a settled streak, just the most recent read. ETH ETFs added $71.4 million on the same day, $115.6 million over five sessions. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $104.7 million in BTC off exchanges in the last 24 hours, the biggest single move being $104.7 million out of OKEx, and $189.9 million in USDT flowed onto Binance, which the desk reads as stablecoin buying power staged and ready rather than spent. The weekly whale trend has been choppier than today's snapshot suggests: two weeks of large inflows to exchanges (+$1.21 billion, +$1.10 billion) followed by two weeks of outflows (-$947.8 million, -$70.0 million), so today's coin-off-exchange move continues the more recent leg but doesn't erase the memory of the earlier one. Stablecoin float itself is essentially flat, down just 0.52% over 30 days at $306.5 billion, so the dry powder pile hasn't materially grown or shrunk.

Sentiment reads Fear at 46, inside its own 30-day range of 25 to 46, meaning today is actually the least fearful the crowd has been in a month even as prices sit near multi-month lows against every trend line. That's the tension: a crowd edging toward neutral, a derivatives book with shorts getting squeezed on the majors and longs crowded in the smaller alts, and traditional-finance money buying on the tape via ETFs while whales quietly walk BTC off exchanges. What to watch from here: whether BTC or ETH can reclaim their 200-day average, whether the ETF's same_direction_days streak extends past two, and whether that long/short ratio on DOGE and XRP unwinds or gets tested again by another liquidation wave like the one that just hit shorts.
